subject: Review and Reform of Governing Ordinances
overview: The commission conducted an extensive review of its governing ordinances, debating its role in grievance handling and structural issues like quorum requirements. The body also voted to endorse the Massachusetts Indigenous Legislative Agenda and discussed member recruitment strategies following the chair's resignation announcement.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the March meeting.

items.title: Review of Governing Ordinances
items.summary: Rob Klein and Diane McDonald presented a distilled report on the city ordinances that establish the commission, detailing its legal remit, officer terms, and membership requirements.

items.title: Quorum and Subcommittee Regulations
items.summary: The commission discussed the challenges of meeting the five-member quorum requirement and the potential for amending rules to empower subcommittees and working groups.

items.title: Grievance Procedures and Enforcement Power
items.summary: Commissioners debated the HRC's role in hearing resident grievances, weighing the value of being heard against the lack of formal enforcement power and the overlap with the city's human resources department.

items.title: Ordinance Overhaul and Council Engagement
items.summary: The commission discussed the necessity of revising the ordinance to resolve inconsistencies and agreed to eventually involve the City Council and solicitor in the reform process.

items.title: 2023 Planning Calendar
items.summary: Approved a motion to dedicate the next meeting to building a formal calendar of events and deliverables for the remainder of 2023.

items.title: Indigenous Legislative Agenda Endorsement
items.summary: Approved the endorsement of the Massachusetts Indigenous Legislative Agenda, which includes five acts regarding mascots, Indigenous Peoples' Day, and heritage protection.

items.title: New Business and Resignation Announcement
items.summary: The commission discussed COVID-19 mask requirements in medical facilities but took no action; additionally, Chair Chelli Keshavan announced her resignation effective June 2023.

items.title: Member Recruitment and Community Outreach
items.summary: The body discussed strategies for recruiting new members at upcoming community events and acknowledged a statewide human rights meeting scheduled for May.
